temperature and GPU load tab for the DeepSeek Harness (dsh) web GUI. btop-style, zero dependencies.
A DeepSeek Harness (dsh) web GUI plugin that shows **live hardware load** right where you work: a se
lf-contained, dependency-free companion to `btop`. Watch your GPU while your local model thinks, wit
hout leaving the chat.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
No restart needed (the web profile reloads live). Reload the browser tab: CPU and GPU load appear in
the session header, and the full **Hardware** tab sits next to Chat / Trajectory. Full details unde
on header, and the full **Hardware** tab sits next to Chat / Trajectory. Full details under Install.
The mini widget in the session header: always visible while you chat. Click it to jump to the full H
get in the session header: always visible while you chat. Click it to jump to the full Hardware tab.
## What it shows
- **CPU** — overall utilisation, a live 60s sparkline, highest temperature reading, and per-core loa
d (every physical core, any count) — with per-thermal-zone detail when there's more than one sensor

- **Memory** — used / available / total with utilisation %
- **GPUs** — one card each: name, tempera
ture, utilisation, power draw, and VRAM (used / total)
Data is sampled host-side on every poll (~0.5 s) and rendered live.
## How it works

- **Host** — a `GET`-only route registered on the dsh web server
(`/plugins/dsh-vitals/data`) that r

eads the OS's own sources
with **no privileged access** and returns JSON.
- **Client** — a single se

lf-contained bundle that polls the route and draws
the panels with inline styles (no CSS pipeline, n

ed bundle that polls the route and draws
the panels with inline styles (no CSS pipeline, no assets).
### Where it shows up
Two access points, both live the moment the plugin is bundled — no setup:

- **A mini widget in the session header**, next to the "⋯" menu: CPU and
per-GPU load as tiny bars,

always visible while you chat. Hover for temps
and VRAM; click to jump to the full tab.
- **A full `

Hardware` tab** next to **Chat** / **Trajectory** at the top of
the conversation view: per-core CPU,
memory, temperatures and every GPU.
### Platform support

Linux, macOS and Windows. Each signal uses the best unprivileged source the OS
offers and hides itse

lf when there is none. Linux is tested live; the macOS and
Windows readers are only checked against

sample output (`npm test`) so far.
Reports from real Macs and Windows machines are very welcome.
| Signal | Linux | macOS | Windows |

| CPU load (overall + per core) | `/proc/stat` | `os.cpus()` | `os.cpus()` |
| Memory | `/proc/memin

fo` | `vm_stat` (counts cache as available, like Activity Monitor) | `os.freemem()` |
| CPU temperat
ure | `/sys/class/thermal` | hidden (needs root) | WMI thermal zones, when the board exposes them (o

ften needs dsh running as admin) |
| NVIDIA GPUs | `nvidia-smi` | `nvidia-smi` | `nvidia-smi.exe` (P

ATH or `NVSMI` folder) |
| Apple / other GPUs | — | `ioreg` utilisation + memory in use | — |

Everything degrades gracefully: a missing source hides that panel or shows a
placeholder instead of

breaking the tab. Any number of GPUs and any CPU core
count is supported.
## Install

Into your dsh **web profile** (`web` below is the profile name; use whichever
profile backs your web

GUI). From a source checkout, use `pnpm dsh` instead of
`npx @deepseek-ai/dsh`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

This installs the package into the profile and adds it to
`dsh.profile.bundles` for you — no manual

`package.json` editing. (No local
`dsh` binary? Run the equivalent by hand from the profile director

y, e.g.
`~/.dsh/profiles/web/`: `pnpm add dsh-vitals`, then add `"dsh-vitals"` to
that `package.json
`'s `dsh.profile.bundles` array yourself.)

The published package ships its built `lib/` output, so no build step runs
on install.

No restart: the shipped `web` profile reloads live, so the plugin shows up under
**Plugins** right a

way. Reload the browser tab — see
Where it shows up above for how to find it.
## Building from source

Requires Node 20+. Dependencies are dev-only (esbuild); the published package
has **zero runtime npm

+. Dependencies are dev-only (esbuild); the published package
has **zero runtime npm dependencies**.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`package.json` declares a `build` script, so `pnpm build` works too.
## Configuration
None. The plugin reads whatever the host exposes; there is no config surface.
## Security

The data route sits outside the dsh web server's `/api` trust fence, so it
enforces that fence itsel

f: `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` requests are rejected
(403) and only `GET`/`HEAD` are served (405 ot
herwise). All sources are read-only.
